html:
Oedipus Rex is a tragedy by Sophocles, probably first staged in Athens around 429 BCE, though the date is uncertain.

A plague is killing the people of Thebes. The oracle of Delphi says it will end only when the killer of the old king, Laius, is found. King Oedipus, proud and clever, leads the hunt himself. Step by step he learns that he is the killer, that Laius was his father, and that his wife Jocasta is his mother. Jocasta hangs herself and Oedipus blinds himself.

The play won only second prize. But Aristotle used it in his Poetics as the model of a tragedy, because the turn of fortune and the moment of discovery happen together. The plague at its start may echo the plague of Athens that had just struck the city. Sigmund Freud took the name of his "Oedipus complex" from it. The story of what happens to Oedipus's children continues in Antigone.
sum: Oedipus Rex is a tragedy by Sophocles, probably first staged in Athens around 429 BCE, though the date is uncertain.
